chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from the one who mentioned it, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, evil character/manners spoils faith just as vinegar spoils honey.
ai.seo_question: How does bad character affect faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the corrosive nature of bad character by comparing it to vinegar spoiling honey, a metaphor widely cited in Shia ethics to show how moral decay undermines the purity of faith. This teaching emphasizes that while faith may remain structurally intact, its spiritual efficacy and sweetness are nullified by poor manners, a concept deeply rooted in the Shia tradition of linking akhlaq (ethics) directly to iman (belief).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The evil mannerism is a spoiler of the Emān just as the vinegar spoils the honey’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Wicked and evil behavior spoils good deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.’”
